item: Row 315 (R789/R792) part 1: a write another process begins after the erase is refused and leaves no salt
summary: Test only. A second process holding its own keyed connection on a real SQLCipher store (idle, mid-transaction, page 1 dirty, pages spilled to the log), with and without the panic wipe's kept descriptors: after the erase its next write is refused ('file is not a database', 'locking protocol', 'malformed'), the data folder is gone, and the store's salt is in none of the files it still holds (read under /proc). A process writing THROUGH the erase is the other half, measured to leave the salt in the unlinked log (5/5 without the hold, 1/5 with it); R792's product change and its test follow.
